study_design: Lifetime prostate cancer analysis among participants in a longitudinal aging study using logistic regression; exposure assessment occurred after diagnosis in 68% of cases, so the abstract does not establish a prospective cohort analysis.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We included in the analysis 454 male participants in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging who were 46 to 92 years old at the time of completion of a food frequency questionnaire.
reason: The abstract evaluates prostate cancer without an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal endpoint. Because most case questionnaires were completed after diagnosis, this is not established as a prospective incident cohort analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Likewise, no significant trends were found for phosphorus, vitamin D, fructose, or animal protein intake.
estimate_classifications.reason: Vitamin D was analyzed in relation to the paper's general prostate cancer outcome; no aggressive endpoint is stated.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The adjusted odds ratio of prostate cancer was 1.26 (95% confidence interval 0.57 to 2.79; P(trend) = 0.73) for men with high dairy intakes compared with those with low dairy intakes.
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported dairy estimate is for prostate cancer generally.
